ki_act-all.title: AI literacy in 15 minutes
ki_act-all.description: A short primer before you practise the 40 AI Act questions.

ki_act-l1-s1.title: Art. 4 AI Act: AI literacy is a provider and deployer duty
ki_act-l1-s1.body: The AI Act obliges providers and deployers of AI systems to take measures, to their best extent, to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy among their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf. This duty is scaled: what counts as "sufficient" depends on the technical knowledge, experience, education, and training of the people involved, as well as the context the AI system is meant to be used in and the persons or groups it will be used on or with. There is no single training programme that fits every role equally — a developer configuring a high-risk system needs a different level of competence than someone who merely reads a chatbot's output. This lesson covers the basic vocabulary you need to make sense of the questions that follow; for exact deadlines and the fine detail of how this duty is worded, check the regulation's own text if you're unsure.

ki_act-l1-s2.title: Four risk tiers, one mnemonic
ki_act-l1-s2.body: Prohibited – high-risk – transparency duty – minimal. The AI Act sorts AI systems roughly into these four tiers, and the tier determines which obligations apply. Prohibited practices (for example certain forms of social scoring or manipulative techniques) are simply banned outright. High-risk systems face the strictest requirements, from risk management to human oversight. Systems subject to a transparency duty (such as chatbots or deepfake generators) must disclose that users are interacting with AI. Everything else — minimal-risk applications — carries no additional obligations under the regulation, though voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged. This four-tier split is the thread running through most of the other question topics: if you can't immediately place a question, start by asking which of the four tiers the system in front of you would fall into.
